title: digitalis purpurea subsp. thapsi
intro: Digitalis purpurea subsp. thapsi, commonly known as Thapsi Foxglove, is a subspecies of the Digitalis purpurea plant, a biennial herb native to Europe and Western Asia. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its cardiotonic and anti-inflammatory properties, which can help to improve heart function and reduce inflammation in the body. The therapeutic actions of Digitalis purpurea subsp. thapsi include its ability to increase cardiac contractility and reduce symptoms of heart failure, as well as its potential to treat conditions such as atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure. The bioactive constituents of this plant include cardenolides, such as digoxin and digitoxin, which are responsible for its therapeutic effects.
